newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian finance minister offers to quit.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian finance minister offers to quit.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas offered to resign on Thursday over allegations that he wrongfully received a loan from a commercial bank which later went bankrupt.
Matiliauskas, 29, took office in November last year as part of the right-wing government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, which swept former Communists from power.
The government says it wants to speed the reforms launched by Lithuania after it quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
A government spokesman said Matiliauskas handed a resgination letter to Vagnorius, saying he wanted to "end political speculation" and avoid damage to the Lithuanian state.
The allegations were not about the bank "but about political fighting", the spokesman quoted the letter as saying.
He said Vagnorius would now consider the resignation offer and then hand it to the president.
The allegations over the loan surfaced in Lithuanian media almost as soon as Matiliauskas was appointed.
The reports said that while Matiliauskas was working in 1993 at now bankrupt Kredito Bankas he took a soft loan and did not repay it.
Matiliauskas says he received the loan under conditions that were current at the time. He also says that he did not use the loan but passed it on to one of the bank's owners.
Matiliauskas also says that in a court decision on Kredito Bankas in 1996 he was not named as a debtor.
Matiliauskas has not had time to prove himself as finance minister in the new government.
He has been in London to negotiate over another credit rating by the IBCA agency after receiving one from New York-based Moody's.
The country announced last week it would launch an ambitious $200 million eurobond, the largest loan it has tried to take from financial markets.
